properties.statement:
UPGRADING THE BINARY DOES NOT REPLACE THE PROCESS THAT SERVES IT, AND EVERY SIGNAL A USER WOULD CHECK LOOKS CURRENT. Reported by Alex (who:alex) on macOS arm64, 2026-08-29, with a clean repro and the authoritative objects read rather than inferred.

MEASURED BY HIM AT THE TIME OF THE CHECK:

    disk binary   ~/.local/bin/reflow2-mcp --version   ->  0.42.0   (mtime 15:20)
    live daemon   pid 66293, started 14:58 (BEFORE that mtime), --serve-shared
    .reflow2/graph.server.json                          ->  "version": "0.39.0"
    HTTP initialize on the rendezvous URL               ->  serverInfo.version 0.39.0
    this session's stdio wrapper                        ->  0.42.0, attached to the 0.39.0 daemon

THREE VERSIONS IN PLAY AT ONCE, and the server log records the attach-probe handshake as 0.42.0 against a process still serving 0.39.0.

REPRO, needing no design content: start a shared server; upgrade the binary in place without stopping it; open a new client session. It attaches to the existing rendezvous and keeps answering as the pre-upgrade version.

🛑 WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A STALE PROCESS USUALLY WOULD, in his words: *"`reflow2-mcp --version` and a new session both look current while every tool call still hits the old surface. The install appeared to succeed."* The mismatch IS discoverable — `graph.server.json`, `served_by.stale`, HTTP `initialize` — but **nothing in the upgrade path surfaces it, and the obvious recovery (restart the session) is the one the docs say does not work**, because `--shared` re-attaches to the same daemon.

⭐ SECOND ENVIRONMENT, SAME DAY, INDEPENDENTLY: the same skew bit this development session SIX TIMES on Linux, from the other direction — `cargo build` replacing the binary under a running daemon rather than an installer doing it. So it is not a macOS quirk and not an installer quirk; it is that NOTHING connects replacing the executable to restarting what serves it. Worst after a `schema/*.yaml` or skill edit, because both are compiled in, so a stale server serves the OLD `describe_schema` and the OLD skill text while every version string reads current.

HIS SUGGESTED FIX, and it is the right shape: *"The install script could restart the shared process after replacing the binary, so the new version is what actually serves."* Read 2026-08-29: `tools/install.sh` has ZERO awareness of a running daemon — no `serve-shared`, `stop-shared`, `kill` or rendezvous handling anywhere in its 179 lines. It replaces the binary at line 119 and never touches the process.

🛑 AND IT GATES THE NEXT RELEASE. Cutting v0.43.0 means every user who upgrades meets this again — including Alex, and including the coworkers he is about to show it to, whose first experience would be a server that serves the previous version while reporting the new one.

🛑 NOT ESTABLISHED: whether SIGTERM to every `--serve-shared` process is safe on a machine where several graphs are served at once. The `--stop-shared` path already prefers SIGTERM precisely so the server removes its own rendezvous on the way out, and a client that finds no rendezvous spawns a fresh one — so the shape is known to work for ONE graph. Nothing has tested it for several at once, and an installer acts machine-wide.

📌 ALSO NOT USED, and he says so himself: `.reflow2/kit-version.json` still read 0.11.0 — the setup-time kit stamp, not the running server. It is not the authority for this question and he did not treat it as one.
